NONE: › said when what you want is extremely unlikely to happen
我要是那麽走運就好了！

example: "You might win first prize." "I should be so lucky."
「你也許會中頭獎。」 「我要是那麽走運就好了。」

NONE: › used to emphasize your agreement or your opinion

example: "Will Beth be there?" "I should hope not! She was so horrible to you."
「貝絲會去嗎？」「我希望不會！她對你態度那麼惡劣。」
"She loved the gift." "I should think she did - you paid enough for it!"
「她很喜歡那件禮物。」「她應該會！你花的錢夠多了。」

NONE: › said when you think what has been suggested is certainly not, or certainly is, the correct and expected thing

example: "I bought her some flowers to say thank you." "I should think so too."
「我買了些花給她表示感謝。」 「當然應該那樣。」
"I don't like to drink more than one bottle of wine in an evening." "I should think not."
「我不喜歡晚上喝超過一瓶的葡萄酒。」 「當然不能。」
"Where's Mark been recently?" "Up to no good, I shouldn't wonder."
「馬克最近去過甚麼地方？」「大概沒去甚麼好地方。」

NONE: › said when you are worried about something unpleasant that might happen or might have happened
我一想到…就惴惴不安，我真不敢想

example: I shudder to think what my parents will say when I tell them I've failed my exams.
我真不敢想如果告訴父母自己沒有通過考試他們會怎麽說。

NONE: › used to admit that something you have said or done was wrong

example: I stand corrected - the date of foundation was 1411, and not 1412 as I had written.
我弄錯了——創立的年代是1411年，而不是我寫的1412年。
